slides.heading: Min Number Of Jumps
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Min Number Of Jumps, a hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Each value is the max jump length from that index; fewest jumps to reach the end.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Each value is the max jump length from that index; fewest jumps to reach the end. Greedy BFS-by-ranges.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Think in BFS levels: each jump extends the farthest reachable index.
slides.narration: Think in BFS levels: each jump extends the farthest reachable index.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: DP: for each i, check all earlier j → O(n²)
Track current range end and farthest reach
slides.narration: A DP checking every earlier index is quadratic. Greedily, think of ranges like BFS levels: within each jump's range, track the farthest reach, and jump when you exhaust the range.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Track the farthest reach and current jump end
2. When we pass the jump end, take another jump
slides.narration: Step by step. First, track the farthest reach and current jump end. Second, when we pass the jump end, take another jump. Third, count jumps until the end.

slides.narration: At index 0, we've used up the range of the current jump. Take jump number 1, extending the reach to index 3.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We track jumps, current end and farthest. For each index before the last, extend farthest; when i reaches end, count a jump and move end to farthest.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Stop before the last index, or you'll count an extra jump.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Explain it as BFS levels over ranges.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Think in BFS levels: each jump extends the farthest reachable index.
slides.narration: To recap Min Number Of Jumps: Think in BFS levels: each jump extends the farthest reachable index. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
